name: Paracetamol
mechanism: Produces analgesic and antipyretic effects; its exact mechanism is not completely established.
contraindications: Severe hepatic impairment requires particular caution
interactions: Warfarin and other medicines may require consideration of interaction depending on use and duration
monitoring: Total exposure from all paracetamol-containing products

name: Ibuprofen
mechanism: Inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes, reducing prostaglandin synthesis.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to ibuprofen or relevant NSAIDs
History of aspirin/NSAID-induced asthma, urticaria or allergic-type reactions
interactions: Anticoagulants
Other NSAIDs
ACE inhibitors or ARBs
Diuretics

name: Amoxicillin
mechanism: Inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins.
uses: Selected ear, nose and throat infections
contraindications: Serious hypersensitivity to amoxicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics
interactions: Warfarin and other anticoagulants may require monitoring
Some bacteriostatic antibiotics may interact pharmacodynamically

name: Azithromycin
mechanism: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit.
uses: Selected respiratory and other bacterial infections
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to azithromycin or other macrolides/ketolides
Previous azithromycin-associated cholestatic jaundice or hepatic dysfunction
adverseEffects: QT prolongation and arrhythmia risk in susceptible patients
interactions: Other medicines that prolong the QT interval
Selected medicines metabolized through hepatic pathways
monitoring: Hepatic adverse effects when clinically appropriate

name: Ceftriaxone
mechanism: Inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins.

adult: Usual adult daily dose: 1–2 g once daily, or divided into two doses, depending on infection and severity.
pediatric: Many pediatric infections: 50–75 mg/kg/day, depending on infection.
Meningitis: initial dose 100 mg/kg, followed by 100 mg/kg/day.
dosage.renalAdjustment: Usually no dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment when usual doses are used.
dosage.hepaticAdjustment: Usually no dosage adjustment is required for hepatic impairment. If significant renal and hepatic dysfunction coexist, caution and closer monitoring are required.
dosage.duration: Common treatment duration is 4–14 days, depending on infection and clinical response.

contraindications: Known serious hypersensitivity to ceftriaxone or relevant cephalosporins
interactions: Important compatibility considerations with calcium-containing IV solutions in specific populations
monitoring: Liver and renal status when clinically appropriate

name: Metformin
mechanism: Reduces hepatic glucose production and improves insulin sensitivity.
uses: Improvement of glycemic control as part of an appropriate treatment plan
adverseEffects: Vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use
Lactic acidosis is a rare but serious adverse effect
interactions: Some drugs affecting renal tubular secretion may alter metformin exposure
Iodinated contrast procedures may require special consideration

name: Insulin
mechanism: Promotes glucose uptake and utilization and suppresses hepatic glucose production.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus when insulin therapy is required
Hyperglycemic emergencies using appropriate insulin protocols
routes: Intravenous for selected preparations and clinical situations
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to the specific insulin preparation or its components
interactions: Other glucose-lowering medicines may increase hypoglycemia risk
Some medicines can alter glucose control or insulin requirements

name: Furosemide
mechanism: Inhibits the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.
adverseEffects: Ototoxicity with excessive exposure or rapid administration
interactions: Other medicines affecting blood pressure
Digoxin and other medicines affected by electrolyte disturbances
Other ototoxic medicines

name: Omeprazole
mechanism: Suppresses gastric acid secretion by inhibiting the gastric H+/K+-ATPase proton pump.
uses: Part of selected Helicobacter pylori eradication regimens
routes: Intravenous in selected formulations and situations
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to omeprazole or relevant proton pump inhibitors
adverseEffects: Long-term use may be associated with specific nutrient and infection-related risks
interactions: Some medicines affected by gastric pH
Selected medicines metabolized through hepatic enzyme pathways
monitoring: Magnesium or vitamin status when clinically indicated

name: Salbutamol
mechanism: Stimulates beta-2 adrenergic receptors, producing relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle.
routes: Oral formulations exist in some settings
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to salbutamol or formulation components
interactions: Other sympathomimetic medicines
Beta-blockers may reduce bronchodilator effect
